citation: Schalk G, McFarland DJ, Hinterberger T, Birbaumer N, Wolpaw JR. BCI2000: a general-purpose brain-computer interface (BCI) system. IEEE Trans Biomed Eng 2004;51(6):1034-1043. EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database, PhysioNet (Goldberger et al. 2000).
record_used: subject S002, baseline run R02 (eyes-closed), channel POz (posterior), first 10 s at 160 Hz (1600 samples) -- the SAME git-tracked vector the SVD-entropy, Petrosian, Renyi, Tsallis, dispersion and fuzzy-entropy cases use.
pipeline: readRDS(eeg_poz_s002r02) -> PhysioEEG::incrementEntropy(dimension, q): take successive differences, embed them, map each increment to a letter = sign x magnitude-class (|increment| quantized in 0..q against the embedding vectors sd), count the increment-word distribution and take its Shannon entropy normalized by (m-1). The reference re-computes it with NeuroKit2 entropy_increment across (dimension, q), via reticulate. Deterministic.
note: The root is the POz channel numeric vector (shared with the SVD-entropy, Petrosian, Renyi, Tsallis, dispersion and fuzzy-entropy cases). Increment entropy (Liu et al. 2016) is a symbolic complexity measure defined on the signals INCREMENTS (successive differences), not its amplitudes: each increment is symbolized by its sign (-, 0, +) and a magnitude class 0..q, and IncrEn is the normalized Shannon entropy of the resulting increment-word distribution. incrementEntropy is a NEW op filling the increment-domain gap (the ecosystem had amplitude-histogram Renyi/Tsallis, NCDF-pattern dispersion, and template-matching sample/fuzzy entropy, but no increment-domain complexity). It reproduces NeuroKit2 entropy_increment BIT-FOR-BIT (max |diff| ~9e-16) across (dimension, q). On real eyes-closed POz EEG it is non-increasing in the embedding dimension (4.27 -> 3.51 -> 3.01 at q=4) and the signal realizes only 33 of the 81 (=(2q+1)^m) possible increment-words -- structured. HONEST: the value depends on (dimension, q); here the NeuroKit2 defaults (m=2, q=4); the reproducible content is the bit-exact family and the word-count structure, not an absolute constant.
